title: Power Platform: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer carry before-and-after values
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap and Microsoft Learn. Its auditing paths, API operations and permissions match the documentation, and it explicitly distinguishes the roadmap target from Learn's earlier start date.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-10-16T19:09:56.
The roadmap describes preventing leaks of sensitive financial, medical and personal information as the change's aim.
claims.quote: To help prevent leaking sensitive customer data from Dataverse audit logs, all customer data is removed before these audit events are sent to Purview activity logging.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs capture create and update events including a column's before-and-after values.
claims.quote: In Dataverse audit logs, create and update events—including a column’s before-and-after values—are captured.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer include before-and-after field change values.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The before-and-after values remain in Dataverse audit logs.
claims.quote: These values remain in Dataverse audit logs, but aren’t sent to Purview activity logging.

claims.claim: Audit events continue flowing to Purview after removal of field-level values.
claims.quote: Audit events will continue to flow to Purview; however, the detailed field-level value changes will be excluded.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving metadata identifying who made changes.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving the date of changes.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving metadata identifying the affected tables.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.claim: Dataverse continues to expose before-and-after changes through its native audit APIs and tables.
claims.quote: Dataverse continues to store and expose before-and-after field changes through its native audit APIs and tables.

claims.claim: The Learn notice gives a start of May 2026, unlike the roadmap's June target.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The roadmap uses the broader wording that all customer data is removed from events before transmission.
claims.quote: all customer data is removed before these audit events are sent to Purview activity logging

claims.claim: The roadmap's Enabled for line says Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users.
claims.quote:
Enabled for:

Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to update downstream workflows to retrieve detailed audit information directly from Dataverse.
claims.quote: Update your monitoring or downstream workflows to retrieve detailed field-level audit information directly from Dataverse, not from Purview.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing monitoring, alerting and reporting solutions that depend on the removed Purview values stop working when the change takes effect.
claims.quote: If you have existing monitoring, alerting, or reporting solutions that depend on before-and-after field change values within Purview audit events, those solutions will stop working once this deprecation takes effect.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The affected examples in Microsoft's notice include anomaly detection rules comparing old and new values.
claims.quote: Rules that compare old/new values for anomaly detection.

claims.claim: The notice lists data pipelines analyzing field-level deltas as affected.
claims.quote: Data pipelines that analyze field-level deltas.

claims.claim: The notice lists custom compliance checks running in Purview as affected.
claims.quote: Custom compliance checks running in Purview.

claims.claim: Microsoft says solutions already using Dataverse audit logs as their source of truth require no changes.
claims.quote: No changes are required if your solution uses Dataverse audit logs as the source of truth.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft says removing field-level values reduces exposure of sensitive information through downstream monitoring and analytics.
claims.quote: Removing detailed field-level values from Purview-bound audit events reduces the risk of exposing sensitive business or personal information through downstream monitoring or analytics systems.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The removal is a platform change that takes effect without an administrator enabling it, represented as defaultState on.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence specifically covering this field-value removal is published, so the change's licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview Dataverse audit before after removal licensing charge meter'. Read the removal notice, activity logs overview and Purview service description; no removal-specific licence found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no meter for this field-value removal.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview Dataverse audit before after removal licensing charge meter'. Read removal notice and activity logs overview; searched Purview service description for Dataverse, before-and-after, field changes and meter. No meter for the removal found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The option to turn on audit logging is visible only when minimum Office licensing requirements are met.
claims.quote: The option to turn on audit logging is only visible when the minimum Office licensing requirements are met.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.claim: Dataverse user access or activity logging is sent to Purview only for production environments.
claims.quote: User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.claim: A System Administrator or System Customizer role, or equivalent permissions, allows auditing configuration changes.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Searching Power Platform activity logs in Purview requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: To view Power Platform activity logs in Microsoft Purview, users need to be assigned either the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.

claims.claim: Viewing Audit Summary requires the Dataverse View Audit Summary privilege.
claims.quote: Users need the View Audit Summary privilege to see the Audit Summary view.

claims.claim: Using the audit change-history messages requires prvReadRecordAuditHistory and prvReadAuditSummary privileges.
claims.quote: To use these messages, ensure you have the prvReadRecordAuditHistory and prvReadAuditSummary privileges.

claims.claim: Environment auditing is controlled at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings > Global Audit Settings > Start Auditing.
claims.quote: Expand Audit and logs and then select Audit settings. ... Select Global Audit Settings to open the Microsoft Dynamics 365 system settings. From there, turn on Start Auditing and select the entities you want to audit.

claims.where: controls[0].api and note; Governance controls: row 1
claims.claim: PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) changes organization settings, with isauditenabled setting environment auditing.
claims.quote: isauditenabled ... Whether auditing is enabled for the environment ... Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment. ... PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Audit Summary is accessible in the model-driven app through Settings > Advanced Settings > System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.
claims.quote: From the app, select the Settings icon on the banner, select Advanced Settings, and then select System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: row 2; Governance guidance
claims.claim: GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/audits(<audit id>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveAuditDetails retrieves audit details including old and new field values.
claims.quote: GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/audits(12869c65-d7d3-ec11-b656-281878f0eba9)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveAuditDetails ... AttributeAuditDetail ... Provides access to old values and new values.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Manage Dataverse auditing says turning off column auditing sends its before-and-after values to Purview as an asterisk.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing for a column, the before-and-after values are sent as an "\*" to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The Dataverse activity logs page says column-level secured fields are sent to Purview activity logging with an asterisk.
claims.quote: Column-level secured fields are sent to Purview activity logging with an asterisk (\*).

claims.claim: The notice describes removal of field values from exported audit events rather than actions on records or users.
claims.quote: Audit events will continue to flow to Purview; however, the detailed field-level value changes will be excluded.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit data can be read through Audit History, Audit Summary or the Web API.
claims.quote: You can view audit logs in the Audit History tab for a single record and in the Audit Summary view for all audited operations in a single environment. You can also retrieve audit logs by using the web API or the SDK for Microsoft .NET.

claims.claim: The Learn notice documents no opt-in or opt-out for this removal.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse Purview before after field values removal opt out restore switch'. Read the removal notice and the activity logs overview; neither documents an opt-in or opt-out for removal of field values.

claims.claim: The existing auditing and retrieval controls do not restore field values to Purview, and the notice gives no restoration step.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse Purview before after field values removal opt out restore switch'. Read removal notice, Manage Dataverse auditing, Configure auditing and Retrieve the history of audited data changes; no control restoring removed values to Purview found.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview path
claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings > Enable SAS Logging in Purview.
claims.quote: Expand the Product list and select Privacy and Security. ... In the Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings section, toggle the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting to On.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview explanation
claims.claim: Enabling SAS logging for a production environment gives Purview auditing access to that environment's activity logs.
claims.quote: A Power Platform system admin or customizer needs to configure auditing in the Power Platform admin center and then turn on the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting for each Power Platform production environment so Microsoft Purview auditing solutions can access the environment's activity logs.

claims.claim: The published Purview customer engagement schema still describes Fields as holding created or updated values.
claims.quote: | Fields | Edm.String | No | JSON of Key Value pair reflecting the values that were created or updated |
